strengths: Principled mechanistic approach using circuit analysis to identify causal components of tense jailbreaking vulnerability, with strong empirical validation of tense encoding in identified heads
Strong empirical results on the targeted problem: reduces ASR from 42-51% to 8-19% while achieving better safety-utility balance than brute-force methods that cause catastrophic over-refusal
Comprehensive evaluation framework across three models with appropriate baselines, multiple metrics, and clear Pareto frontier visualization
Lightweight and efficient solution with scaling vectors fusible into weights for zero inference overhead
Good reproducibility with extensive hyperparameters, architectural details, and promised code release; includes ablations and mechanistic verification
weaknesses: Severely limited scope: method addresses only tense jailbreaking. No evaluation against other attack types (adversarial suffixes, semantic jailbreaks, compositional attacks) or transfer to related linguistic variations (other temporal structures), fundamentally limiting impact and practical relevance

Inadequate evaluation dataset: only 100 jailbreaking prompts with single judge (GPT-4.1) and no statistical significance testing. Small sample size raises serious generalization concerns and results lack confidence intervals/multiple runs

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: core claims that vulnerable heads 'signal historical inquiry' to downstream mechanisms are speculative rather than rigorously validated. No explanation of why these heads encode tense or why scaling outperforms alternatives. Different post-ASGUARD patterns across models (only Llama shows consistent improvements) undermines generality claims

Preventative fine-tuning lacks theoretical grounding: core innovation justified only by informal regularization arguments. No evidence model learns 'non-vulnerable pathways' vs. overfitting to intervention. No ablation demonstrating its necessity or explaining how detached scaling vectors maintain behavior

Over-refusal trade-off inadequately addressed: ASGUARD substantially increases over-refusal (Llama 28.9%→66.8%, Qwen 12.9%→70.5%, Gemma 70.5%→88.0%)—representing 66pp increase for Qwen with unclear practical deployment implications

No robustness evaluation: does not test adversarial circumvention through tense variants, mixed tense, implicit temporal references, or adaptive attacks. Unclear if defense is fragile to minor perturbations

Model-dependent results unexplained: Gemma achieves only 50% relative reduction vs. 83% for Llama/Qwen. Post-ASGUARD linear probe patterns differ across models. Paper acknowledges but provides no principled understanding of when/why method succeeds

Circuit analysis technical concerns: threshold parameters τ and top-n appear arbitrary with no sensitivity analysis. Faithfulness validation incomplete—doesn't verify minimality or sufficiency of circuits
Missing ablations on component importance and no investigation of why 'Only Scaling' fails catastrophically on Gemma (drops to 50.3% MMLU vs 72.2% baseline)
Limited generalization: method fails on small models (Phi-3-mini); no systematic evaluation across architectures (MoE, distilled, synthetic-pretrained), limiting transferability claims

strengths: Well-motivated mechanistic approach using circuit analysis to identify tense-vulnerable attention heads responsible for the jailbreak vulnerability
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple strong baselines (SFT, DPO, RepE, CB, RepBend) across four different LLMs
Excellent Pareto frontier analysis demonstrating safety-utility trade-off and showing ASGUARD achieves superior balance compared to brute-force methods
Thorough mechanistic validation through linear probe analysis (73-77% accuracy) and ablation studies with random heads confirming specificity of identified circuits
Strong practical results: reduces tense jailbreak ASR from 42% to 8% on Llama while preserving MMLU scores and reducing over-refusal
Out-of-domain testing with GCG and LogiBreak attacks demonstrating some generalization beyond tense jailbreaking
Clear presentation with extensive reproducibility details and promise to release code/datasets
weaknesses: Severely limited scope: primary evaluation on only tense jailbreaking with just 100 prompts; GCG/LogiBreak are secondary confirmatory tests rather than core focus

Lack of cross-model generalization: identified vulnerable heads are completely different across models (e.g., different heads for Llama vs Qwen), requiring expensive circuit discovery per model with no demonstration of transfer
Limited model coverage: only 7-9B instruction-tuned open-source models; no evaluation on larger models (13B+), different architectures (MoE), or closed-source LLMs, making scalability unclear

Questionable circuit discovery robustness: small training set (100 prompts), arbitrary threshold selection (τ ∈ [0.03, 0.1]), no sensitivity analysis, and no investigation of robustness to different prompt sets

Incremental novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (circuit analysis from Elhage et al., activation scaling from Lee et al., preventative fine-tuning from Chen et al.) rather than fundamental innovation

Mechanistic claims not fully supported: linear probe accuracy of 73-77% is moderate; claim about adversarial suffixes suppressing refusal direction lacks direct evidence; Section 6.2 shows inconsistent post-ASGUARD behavior across models
Remaining practical concerns: even with ASGUARD, Qwen2.5 shows 70.5% over-refusal rate on OR-Bench-Hard; evaluation relies on GPT-4.1 judge creating dependency on proprietary model
Missing key analyses: no sensitivity to prompt set selection, no computational cost discussion, limited failure case analysis, unclear generalization principles for other attack types

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a concrete documented vulnerability (tense jailbreaking generalization gap) with clear practical importance
Principled mechanistic approach using circuit analysis (EAP-IG) to identify causal components, with clever False-to-True vs Always-False circuit differentiation

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 diverse models with multiple evaluation dimensions (targeted refusal, general refusal, over-refusal, general knowledge) and strong baselines including recent methods
Strong empirical results achieving Pareto-optimal safety-utility balance (42%→8% ASR on Llama while maintaining MMLU and reducing over-refusal vs. methods achieving 0% ASR)

Excellent mechanistic verification through linear probe classification (73-76% accuracy confirming tense encoding), dot product analysis, random head ablation controls, and post-intervention circuit analysis
Innovative three-stage design combining circuit identification, lightweight channel-wise scaling, and preventative fine-tuning that demonstrates superior performance
High reproducibility with promised code/data release and detailed hyperparameter documentation across all experiments
weaknesses: Limited scope: method is specifically engineered for tense jailbreaking; while GCG/LogiBreak results shown, circuit discovery and head identification are attack-specific, requiring expensive per-vulnerability analysis without a general framework for scaling to multiple vulnerabilities

Significant architecture-dependent performance variation with concerning results (Gemma-2 'Only Scaling' drops MMLU from 72.2 to 50.3); acknowledged limitations on distilled/MoE models and small models like Phi-3-mini substantially limit practical applicability

Circuit analysis hyperparameters (threshold τ ∈ [0.1, 0.03], ig-step=100, top-n=5000) lack principled justification or sensitivity analysis; circuit discovery requires advance knowledge of vulnerability and uses only 100 prompts without adequacy validation

Preventative fine-tuning mechanism poorly justified: claim that neutralizing vulnerable heads during training yields permanent robustness lacks theoretical grounding; 'implicit regularization' stated without analysis; design choices (over-scaling) appear ad-hoc

Statistical rigor concerns: no confidence intervals, significance testing, or multiple runs; GPT-4.1 as sole judge for ASR without bias discussion; 'Pareto-optimal' only relative to tested baselines; refusal dataset construction undocumented

Limited component novelty: circuit analysis (Elhage et al. 2021), activation scaling (Lee et al. 2025), and preventative fine-tuning (Chen et al. 2025) are from prior work; main contribution is application-specific combination

Missing critical ablations: no study of prompts needed for circuit discovery, scaling vector magnitude sensitivity, cross-model transferability of scaling vectors, or comparison of circuit discovery methods

Practical scalability unclear: computational cost of circuit analysis not reported; no demonstration that approach scales to systematically addressing multiple vulnerabilities; represents 'surgical patching' rather than fundamental safety improvement
